title: Medical LLM Metacognition Is Multidimensional: A MetaMedQA Reanalysis of Confidence, Missing-Answer Recognition, and Unknown-Answer Detection

live_model.evidence: Abstract: "Two GPT-family models, gpt-4.1-nano and gpt-5.5, were evaluated on 1373 MetaMedQA items using structured outputs containing an answer, numerical confidence, and a more-information-needed judgment. gpt-4.1-nano achieved 56.4% accuracy..."

prompt.location: Abstract only describes the output contract ("structured outputs containing an answer, numerical confidence, and a more-information-needed judgment"); the input prompt template itself is not present
prompt.note: The text_path for this record captured only the Zenodo landing page (title, abstract, file listing for "Medical LLM Metacognition Is Multidimensional.pdf", 714.9 kB) - not the full paper body, so the methods/prompt appendix could not be read.

claim.location: Abstract: "gpt-4.1-nano achieved 56.4% accuracy, mean confidence of 79.7%, Brier score of 0.318, expected calibration error of 0.276, and AUROC2 of 0.582"

data.source: MetaMedQA (public medical-QA benchmark); this reanalysis itself is openly published on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.20186339)

notes: Everything in the abstract points to a clean, reproducible role-S evaluation (also reports missing-answer recall 19.1% and unknown/unanswerable recall 25.9% for gpt-4.1-nano), but the extracted text is only the Zenodo record's landing-page metadata, not the full PDF, so the exact prompt/structured-output schema could not be verified. gpt-5.5 (84.9% accuracy on the same 1373 items) is also evaluated but is outside the tracked still-callable identifier list.
